clue.text: Do up theatre about five in the morning

indicators.note: the theatre word goes about, round the outside of, the next two pieces

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
V is the Roman numeral five
AM, ante meridiem, marks the morning hours

explanation.surface: Someone renovates a theatre at five in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the theatre word round the other two pieces; 'Do up' is to renovate, not to fasten.
explanation.definitionFit: To do up a building or a show is to renovate or overhaul it, a synonym.

clue.text: Fine choreographer tackles forerunner of foxtrot

indicators.note: the phrase takes on, grips the letters running across its two words, so the answer sits inside it

explanation.surface: A first-rate choreographer takes on a foxtrot routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like praise for the choreographer; its last letter starts the answer, which spans the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for E comes immediately before Foxtrot for F.

clue.text: Animal found by learner driver in winding Lima road, squashed

indicators.note: a winding road twists, so the letters of the place and road are turned about
squashed letters are crushed out of shape into a new order

parts.note: a learner driver carries an L plate

explanation.surface: A creature meets a learner driver on a twisting road in Lima and gets run over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' and 'squashed' both signal rearranging L plus LIMAROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: This armoured South American mammal is one example of an animal, plausibly flattened on a road.

clue.text: Ignore idiot in lead over 26

indicators.note: in a down entry the first part is placed over, above, the next
the idiot sits in, inside, the chemical symbol for lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
an ass is a fool
the answer to 26 across is the NATO code word for Y

explanation.surface: Someone is told to disregard a fool who leads a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is YANKEE, which stands for the letter Y in the NATO alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass someone or something by is to overlook or disregard them, an idiom.

clue.text: Pope briefly hosts American twice in private

indicators.note: the assembled piece is written two times over
the pope's abbreviation hosts, holds inside, the American abbreviation

parts.note: HH, His Holiness, is the short form of the pope's title

explanation.surface: The pope, in short, entertains an American guest twice, behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope briefly' is His Holiness abbreviated; 'hosts' puts the American inside, and 'twice' doubles the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept secret and confidential is private, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Cowboy spoils gaps in school day

indicators.note: the phrase is spoilt, wrecked, so its letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A cowboy wrecks the free periods of a school day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' rearranges all fifteen letters of GAPS IN SCHOOL DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a fictional Western hero of novels, films and television, a famous example of a cowboy.

clue.text: Small bed on this irritated Caledonian

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: irritated suggests the word is agitated, stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scot is annoyed at being put on a small bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irritated' rearranges THIS into TISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland, so a Caledonian is a native of that country.

clue.text: Frequent hard worker steals uniform

parts.note: H is short for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: the worker steals, takes in, the uniform letter

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A tough labourer keeps pinching uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frequent' is the verb, to visit often, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt a place is to visit it often, as a regular does; both are verbs.

clue.text: Overcame stable director injecting horse

indicators.note: the horse word is injected, put inside, the first two pieces

parts.note: sure means steady or stable
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: A racing-stable boss got the better of things by drugging a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like a horse yard but is the adjective SURE; MOUNT goes into SURED.
explanation.definitionFit: To surmount a difficulty is to overcome it, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: OK to take drink after hitch?

indicators.note: the drink comes after the hitching word

parts.note: to thumb is to hitch a lift
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Is it all right to have a drink after a snag?
explanation.walkthrough: 'hitch' looks like a problem but is the verb, hitchhiking with the thumb.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised-thumb gesture signals approval, so the phrase means agreement or okay.

clue.text: Guide without staff or work

indicators.note: the guiding word goes without, loses, the staff word

parts.note: to manoeuvre is to steer or guide
to man is to staff

explanation.surface: A guide lacking a stick, or else a job.
explanation.walkthrough: MANOEUVRE (guide) less MAN (staff) leaves the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a body of work, or a single work, of an artist or writer.

clue.text: Initiate bold moves in weak state

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase move into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone frail makes the first bold moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges INITIATE BOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Debility is weakness, so this noun names the condition of being weakened.

clue.text: Good man holding tiny bottle loved one

indicators.note: the good man abbreviation holds the tiny word inside

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
wee means tiny in Scots
bottle is British slang for courage, as is heart

explanation.surface: A decent man clutching a little bottle is someone's beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' looks like a container but is slang for nerve, HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart is a beloved partner, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A worn-out old loco initially missing from station

indicators.note: the initial letters of the three words are taken

explanation.surface: A tired old locomotive has gone missing from the station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' means a soldier's post; absent without leave is military.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent without leave means a soldier has deserted their post or station.

clue.text: Express knows about unit that makes flight easier

indicators.note: to express a word is to say it out, so it is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the word knows, said out, gives the body part's spelling
C is short for circa, about
one is a unit

explanation.surface: A fast train knows about a part that helps aircraft along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a train but signals the spoken word.
explanation.definitionFit: The tapering front of a rocket or aircraft reduces drag, easing its passage through the air.

clue.text: Tin protects a river craft

indicators.note: the tin surrounds, protects, the next two pieces

parts.note: a can is a tin
the Tamar is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall

explanation.surface: A tin shields a river boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protects' wraps the tin round 'a' plus the river, which splits the tin after its first letter. The Tamar divides Devon from Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled boat, an example of a craft.

clue.text: Author is on TV, restless about Spanish article

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, round, the article
restless letters will not stay still and shift into a new order

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A writer appears on television, fidgeting while discussing a Spanish piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restless' rearranges IS ON TV into NOVIST, and 'about' wraps that round the Spanish article.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of novels is a kind of author.

clue.text: Mike tours English zoos from a bygone age

indicators.note: the letters tour, go round, into a new order

parts.note: mic is short for microphone, also called a mike

explanation.surface: Mike visits English zoos to see ancient creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tours' rearranges MIC, E and ZOOS.
explanation.definitionFit: The geological era of the dinosaurs, describing something from the remote past.

clue.text: Millions extracted from newspaper unions

indicators.note: the millions abbreviation is pulled out of the paper

parts.note: The Times is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Millions are drained from a paper by trade unions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unions' means bonds or links, not trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonds or links joining things together, as in family connections.

clue.text: Humour Buffalo Bill lassoing writer

indicators.note: the showman's surname lassoes, encircles, the writer

parts.note: Buffalo Bill was William Cody
me is the setter, the writer of the clue

explanation.surface: Buffalo Bill ropes in a writer for a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is the setter, ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedy is the craft of humour, a synonym.

clue.text: Result of ten drums Thor hammered?

definitions.text: Result of ten drums Thor hammered?

indicators.note: hammered letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: What follows when the thunder god beats ten drums?
explanation.walkthrough: Thor is the Norse god of thunder, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor's hammering on drums would produce a storm of thunder, the whole clue as a picture.

clue.text: Animal in Africa, one invading cities

indicators.note: the one letter invades, goes into, the city abbreviations

parts.note: NY and LA are New York and Los Angeles
a means one

explanation.surface: An African beast storms two cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cities' supplies New York and Los Angeles by their usual abbreviations; 'invading' slots the one between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa, an example of an African animal.

clue.text: Philanthropist's thank-you note

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A donor's note of thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Tate, the sugar magnate, founded the London gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The sugar refiner Henry Tate gave his art collection to found the gallery, a named philanthropist.

clue.text: Fruit in perfect condition around island state

parts.note: a haw is the fruit of hawthorn

indicators.note: the perfect condition goes around the island letter

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written as AI

explanation.surface: Fruit in prime condition around an island state.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, read as letters AI, goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawaii is the fiftieth of the United States, an example of a state.

clue.text: Reserve the best dessert

parts.note: to ice, put on ice, is to keep in reserve
the cream is the best part

explanation.surface: Keep back the finest pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on ice' means to hold in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen sweet served at the end of a meal is a common dessert.

clue.text: Furtive little paddler with time to board launch

indicators.note: the duck and time board, get inside, the launch word

parts.note: to shy is to throw or launch
a teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: A small duck gets aboard a boat in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launch' looks like a boat but is the verb SHY, to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means sly and secretive, a synonym of furtive.

clue.text: Bet Europeans pursue tug

indicators.note: the Europeans follow, pursue, the tug word

parts.note: a yank is a sharp tug
E is short for European, twice

explanation.surface: Wager that Europeans will chase a tugboat.
explanation.walkthrough: A YANKEE is a bet of eleven wagers on four selections.
explanation.definitionFit: In British betting this is a multiple wager covering eleven bets on four horses.
